mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation that typically triggers monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 310, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is greater than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC between UNRATE change and 5-day returns is less than -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) and strong industrial production (INDPRO > 105) indicates robust economic demand, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5% and INDPRO > 105, or the Rank IC between the interaction term (UNRATE*INDPRO) and 20-day returns is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, high GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) signals overheating and impending monetary tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC between GDPC1 growth and 20-day returns is greater than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and strong economic growth, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above its 3-year rolling average, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 60-day returns is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1250.0 thousand units signals weakening demand for residential construction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1250.0, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 20-day returns is greater than -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS > 158000) and elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals an overheating economy and aggressive monetary tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 158000 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC between the interaction term (PAYEMS*FEDFUNDS) and 20-day returns is less than -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary easing cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS < 5.0% and a 3-month decline > 0.1 percentage points), the central bank's accommodative policy compresses discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 5.0% and FEDFUNDS decline > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of monetary easing cycles (FEDFUNDS < 5.0% and decline > 0.1pp in 3 months), or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS decline and 20-day returns is less than 0.03.
